client_requirement: A vanilla 26.1.2 real client must connect to playable.toml through the repo-native Gradle runClient adapter; protocol harnesses do not satisfy this gate, and prepared artifacts are not passing evidence.

steps: Start Solaris with playable.toml through the runner.
Connect one vanilla 26.1.2 client to 127.0.0.1:25565.
Wait until the client is in Play state on the generated seed-0 world.
Capture a screenshot after chunks and hotbar are visible.
expected_observations: Client reaches Play state without disconnect.
Generated terrain and player HUD render in the screenshot.
observations.json records client_gate=agent-run-real-client.

steps: From generated spawn, walk to a naturally generated tree.
Break logs without debug commands or starter-kit injection.
Pick up drops, craft planks, sticks, a crafting table, and a wooden pickaxe.
Place and open the crafting table, then craft or verify a basic tool.
expected_observations: Log break, item drop, pickup, inventory, hotbar, and recipe flow converge in the real client.
Crafting table placement/opening works without ghost blocks.
Screenshots show the survival state after tool crafting.

The placed crafting table persists at the recorded marker coordinates.
The crafted wooden pickaxe remains in player inventory after rejoin.

steps: Run the playable gate wrapper with the default Gradle runClient adapter.
Stay connected for a 20-minute survival session on playable.toml.
Walk, jump, collide, break/place common blocks, pick up drops, craft the wood-to-tool loop, and rejoin after a clean restart.
Capture screenshots for the join, crafting/tool state, and post-restart state.
expected_observations: No server crash, client disconnect, catastrophic tick stalls, or unrecovered movement desync during the 20-minute window.
Break/place/drop/pickup/crafting-table actions are visible through the real client.
Save/restart/rejoin preserves the edited world and player inventory.
observations.json result is passed only for agent-run-real-client evidence.
